why: The tool takes no arguments at all (server.py:308) -- it just calls close_browser() -- so there is no caller-controlled input to trace to any sink.

linkedin_username is passed through normalize_person_identifier (identifiers.py), which refuses path syntax, dot-segments, control bytes and double-encoding before building the profile URL, and the invite URL is built with quote_plus(username); the write itself (extractor.py connect_with_person, ~2440-2620) is further gated on a structural has_invite_anchor signal and note text is delivered via Playwright locator.fill(), never interpolated into JS, so there is no injection path and the destructive action is exactly the tool's advertised, confirmation-hinted purpose.

company_name goes through normalize_company_identifier and company_page_url (quote(...,safe='')) and the optional keywords filter is quote_plus-encoded before being appended to the URL query (extractor.py get_company_employees, ~3299-3313), so no path/query injection is possible.
company_name is normalized with normalize_company_identifier before company_page_url() builds the /posts/ URL (tools/company.py:138-140); no other caller-controlled input reaches a sink.

company_name is normalized via normalize_company_identifier inside scrape_company (extractor.py:3205-3218) before building any URL; sections is filtered through parse_company_sections against the fixed COMPANY_SECTIONS allowlist, so nothing caller-controlled reaches the navigation URL unescaped.

thread_id is passed through normalize_thread_id/messaging_thread_url (quote(...,safe='')); the username path resolves through normalize_person_identifier and then only matches thread refs whose page-rendered participant name equals the (already-normalized) input, with the SPA URL built by LinkedIn's own click handler, not by string interpolation of caller input.
The only caller-controlled argument is num_posts, a pydantic-bounded int (1-50) that only controls a scroll-count loop; there is no string argument that reaches a URL, selector or command.
The only caller-controlled argument is limit, a pydantic-bounded int (1-50) used only to size a scroll/click loop; no string input reaches a URL or command sink.

job_id is passed through normalize_job_id, which requires the value to reduce to digits (or the numeric tail of a /jobs/view/ slug) before job_view_url quote()s it into the navigation URL (extractor.py scrape_job, 3337-3344); a non-numeric value is rejected with InvalidReferenceError rather than reaching the browser.

The tool takes no username argument (it always navigates to the fixed /in/me/ URL and reads the resolved username back from page.url); sections is filtered through parse_person_sections against the fixed PERSON_SECTIONS allowlist before use, so no caller string reaches a sink unescaped.

linkedin_username is normalized via normalize_person_identifier inside scrape_person (extractor.py:2029-2055), which refuses dot-segments, control bytes, backslashes and double percent-encoding, and person_profile_url() then quote()s it; sections is filtered against the fixed PERSON_SECTIONS allowlist by parse_person_sections.

The only caller-controlled argument is max_pages, a pydantic-bounded int (1-10) controlling a pagination loop over a fixed URL (https://www.linkedin.com/my-items/saved-jobs/); no string input reaches a URL, selector or command.

linkedin_username is normalized via normalize_person_identifier before person_profile_url() quotes it (extractor.py get_sidebar_profiles, 2645-2658); the subsequent 'Show all' navigations use an href read out of LinkedIn's own rendered sidebar DOM (extractor.py ~2722-2762), not caller input, so the only externally supplied argument never reaches an unguarded sink.
keywords is quote_plus-encoded into the search URL query string (extractor.py search_companies, 4514-4523); no other caller input exists.
keywords is quote_plus-encoded into the ?searchTerm= query parameter (extractor.py search_conversations, 4871-4889); limit is a pydantic-bounded int controlling only a click-enumeration loop.

keywords/location are quote_plus-encoded and every filter (date_posted, job_type, experience_level, work_type, sort_by) is mapped through a fixed lookup table with the mapped/raw value still quote_plus-encoded or restricted to comma-normalized tokens before being appended to the URL (extractor.py _build_job_search_url, 3717-3752); max_pages is a bounded int.

keywords/location are quote_plus-encoded, network tokens are validated against a fixed allowlist ('F'/'S'/'O') raising FilterValidationError otherwise, and current_company must match ^[0-9]+$ or the call raises before any URL is built (extractor.py search_people, 4438-4489); no unescaped caller input reaches the URL.

keywords is quote_plus-encoded and date_posted is passed through a fixed token map before quote-encoding (extractor.py _build_content_search_url, 4548-4572); max_pages is a bounded int controlling scroll depth only.

linkedin_username is normalized via normalize_person_identifier before person_profile_url() quotes it, profile_urn is quote_plus-encoded into the compose URL, and the message body is delivered via page.keyboard.type() (real keystroke events on the focused contenteditable box), never interpolated into a JS string or selector (extractor.py send_message, 4920-5089), so there is no code-injection or DOM-selector-breakout path; sending itself is the tool's advertised, destructiveHint-annotated, confirm_send-gated purpose.
